planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
FORBIDDING THE FENCE FILES to keep the row small, as the old plan did. Rejected - it is not achievable. The exclusion is derived from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`, so it moves the moment the kind becomes operator-only. A plan that forbids the files still causes the change; it just leaves the worker holding unexplained red.

CALLING THE INTERIM "MCP-ADVERTISED". Rejected on the same measurement: the fence and the payload key land in one commit, so no landed HEAD advertises this kind over MCP. That matters because the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential - an advertised operator kind means an agent arrives AS the operator - but here the window does not exist.

A SYNCHRONOUS REGISTRY ENTRY, as DoD 1's wording implies. Rejected: `CommandHandler` returns `ServiceOutcome`, and a rollback that redeploys an image and probes health cannot. `deployment.deploy` is already in the async seam for exactly this reason; rollback follows it. This is the same defect that forced task-04b3ce7e's re-plan, and it is worth not repeating.

WRITING A PARALLEL ROSTER TEST (rail 3). Rejected: the bidirectional set-equality and the per-transport sweeps auto-generate this kind's cases. Moving their pins IS the work; an added arm is duplicate coverage and the tell is an `it(` counter that had to move.

THE DEFECT: the old plan called the interim state "MCP-advertised" and FORBADE the fence files, while its own step 2(3) added `deployment.rollback` to `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`. mcp-tool-allowlist.ts DERIVES the exclusion from that set:
  ...[...OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS].filter((kind) => !MCP_REACHABLE_OPERATOR_KINDS.has(kind)).sort(),
and its own comment states the contract: "Deriving keeps `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` the single place the human-only class is stated: a kind that becomes operator-only leaves the MCP roster with no edit here." So THE EXCLUSION AND ITS COUNT PINS MOVE WITH THE WIRING WHETHER THE PLAN NAMES THEM OR NOT. Two consequences: (1) there is no "MCP-advertised interim" to close - the fence lands in the same commit as the payload key, by construction; (2) forbidding the asserting files does not prevent the change, it only hides which files go red. They are named in this plan.

ROLLBACK IS ASYNC, NOT A SYNC REGISTRY ENTRY - measured, and it differs from what DoD 1 implies. `deployment.deploy` is ALREADY in the async seam: daemon-command-async-entries.ts:23 imports `DEPLOYMENT_DEPLOY_COMMAND_KIND` from `./deployment/deploy-target-contracts.js`, :49 comments that it "runs `docker build`, an optional `docker save | ssh docker load`, and a...", and :56 has it in the `AsyncCommandKind` union. The rollback effect (task-da60dc4b) redeploys a previous image and probes health - the same shape - and `CommandHandler` is `(context) => ServiceOutcome`, synchronous, which cannot express it. DoD 1's "a registry entry" is satisfied by the async entry; say so in the completion record rather than forcing a sync handler.
Note this also means `deploy-target-contracts.ts` HAS been adopted and imported since I filed task-358b6ec8 - re-measure rather than assuming it is still orphaned.

`deployment.rollback` IS COMPLETELY UNWIRED: `git grep -n "deployment.rollback" -- apps/daemon/src` returns ZERO. All of DoD 1 is real work.

SIZE HAZARD: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts is 392 LINES against a 400 hard cap. Adding a kind is ~7 lines and would cross it. Pack entries onto shared lines the way the file already does, or move the family entry into daemon-command-families.ts - which is already in this plan's roster for exactly that reason.

PINS ALREADY RECONCILED BY SIBLINGS - DO NOT DOUBLE-BUMP (the governor's explicit instruction): `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy` pins were moved by task-54b74b80 and task-04b3ce7e. This row moves the pins for ONE new kind only. Rail 4 and the governor both say the same thing: take every number from the PRINTED expected-vs-received at the final gate, never from a plan.
